units.title: A rollout moves through internal, canary and general availability
units.claim: A rollout has three stages: internal (staff accounts only, usually one working day with no minimum), canary (a small share of real traffic) and general availability (everyone, in steps of 25%, 50% and 100%); every move is recorded in the rollout tool.
units.explanation: The unchanged concept: identical in v1 (u6–u11) and v2 (u37–u42). An update must leave its card alone.

omission.reason: The frame every other step hangs on.

units.title: Canary holds the flag at 5% of requests for a minimum time (30 minutes in v1, 60 in v2)
units.claim: During canary the flag is on for 5% of requests, picked at random per request, and stays there for at least 30 minutes in the first version and at least 60 minutes in the revision, so the metrics cover a full traffic cycle of the slowest endpoint; a manual change restarts the window.
units.explanation: The edited explanation: v2 rewords every sentence of the section (u43–u46 for u12–u15) and changes one number, 30 → 60 minutes. Same idea, so one knowledge id; the canvas card must end up with 60.
mustPreserve: at least / no less than (a minimum, not a fixed duration)

paraphrase.note: The percentage and the duration stay exact for the version shown.

units.title: Canary advances only through the gate: the metrics check (v1), plus on-call approval (v2)
units.claim: A flag advances from canary to general availability only when the automated metrics check passes (error rate and p95 latency against the previous 7 days); in the revision the on-call engineer must also approve the move, and may decline it while an incident is open.
units.explanation: The changed dependency: in v1 the move depends on the metrics check alone (u16); in v2 on the metrics check AND on-call approval (u47, u50). The rest of the section is unchanged (u17–u19 = u48, u49, u51).

units.title: Every flag needs a kill switch that turns it off within 1 minute
units.claim: Every flag must have a kill switch that turns it off within 1 minute; it is tested in staging before canary (a flag without a tested kill switch cannot enter canary), anyone on the owning team may use it without approval, and turning the flag back on restarts the rollout from the internal stage.
units.explanation: Unchanged between versions (u20–u24 = u52–u56). Its card was edited by the user on the v1 canvas (reconcile.json userEdits): the edit must survive the update.
mustPreserve: cannot enter canary without a tested kill switch

units.title: During the ramp-up the owner watches the error dashboard and pages on-call if errors rise
units.claim: While the flag ramps up, the owner watches the error dashboard (flagged and unflagged requests side by side) and pages the on-call engineer if errors rise, until the flag has been at 100% for one hour.
units.explanation: Same idea in both versions, but v2 splits u25 into two sentences (u57, u58): an ambiguous unit match. Card-level reconcile should send it to review rather than rewrite it.

units.title: A flag fully on for 30 days is removed from the code
units.claim: A flag that has been fully on for 30 days is removed from the code; the owner opens a cleanup ticket at 100%, and flags past the deadline appear in the weekly stale-flag report.
units.explanation: The removed concept: only in v1 (u28–u31). After the update its card's removal must be proposed, not kept silently.

omission.reason: Present in v1, so it is on the v1 canvas.

units.title: Before general availability, the owner rehearses a rollback once in staging
units.claim: Before general availability the owner rehearses a rollback once in staging (switch off, confirm the old behaviour, switch on), records it in the rollout tool, and it takes about 10 minutes with no approval.
units.explanation: The new concept: only in v2 (u61–u63). The update must add it.

omission.reason: Not in v1, so not on the v1 canvas; the update adds it.

mustNotClaim.claim: After the v2 update, canary lasts at least 30 minutes.
mustNotClaim.why: v2 raises the minimum to 60 minutes; the old number is stale.

mustNotClaim.claim: After the v2 update, the metrics check alone lets a flag leave canary.
mustNotClaim.why: v2 adds on-call approval as a second condition.

mustNotClaim.claim: After the v2 update, flags are removed 30 days after reaching 100%.
mustNotClaim.why: v2 no longer contains the cleanup rule.

mustNotClaim.claim: The v1 canvas requires on-call approval to leave canary.
mustNotClaim.why: That condition only exists in v2.
